title: Similar Triangles

findings.finding: Extend the nested-triangle question by comparing increases in corresponding side lengths.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up connects the scale factor with the difference between corresponding lengths.
findings.assumptions: Students complete p7-q7-b first. The extension adds only subtraction and ratio comparison to the methods that question already requires.

repair.proposal: Append to p7-q7: c Find DE. Answer: 4 cm. d Find CD:DE. Answer: 2:1. e Find BD:(AE−BD). Answer: 2:1. f Explain why the ratios in d and e are equal. Expected answer: each larger corresponding length is 1.5 times the smaller length, so each increase is half the smaller length.

findings.doneWhen: The follow-up appears after p7-q7-b, with each question presented as a separate part.

contextQuestions.question: Have students previously been taught to find unknown corresponding lengths using a scale factor or a proportion, for example in Properties of Geometrical Figures — A: Similarity? protectedGroups.observation: Parallel lines can establish triangle similarity in both intersecting and nested configurations before corresponding sides are used.
protectedGroups.varies: Intersecting versus nested triangles, alternate versus corresponding angles, and scale direction.
protectedGroups.invariant: Parallel sides establish equal angles, followed by a corresponding-side calculation.

protectedGroups.observation: The same common-angle and corresponding-angle proof works after changing the orientation.
protectedGroups.invariant: A segment parallel to one side creates a smaller triangle sharing a vertex with the larger triangle.
